subject: Television & Streaming
title: Representation Still Matters
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Representation Still Matters.

hook.text: A UCLA study found that in 2023, people of color held 39 percent of lead roles on TV. Progress, but not parity.

buildup.text: Behind the camera, the gap is wider. Only 20 percent of show creators are people of color. Writers' rooms lag further.

discovery.text: Children who see characters like themselves on screen develop higher self-esteem and broader aspirations.

twist.text: Streaming increased representation on screen but economic pressures now threaten the gains. Diversity hiring slowed.

climax.text: Representation is not a trend—it's infrastructure. When diverse voices shape stories, everyone's world gets bigger.

punchline.text: You can't dream of what you've never seen on screen.

quiz.question: Why does behind-the-camera representation matter as much as on-screen diversity?
options: Diverse creators shape the stories told, ensuring authentic perspectives rather than surface-level casting
